title: Round 5 — Which Région? (a photo tour of all 13)

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: A vast French Renaissance château with many towers and chimneys
questions.imageCredit: Château de Chambord · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: The Château de Chambord, the grandest of the Loire châteaux, built for François I.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: White chalk sea cliffs with a natural stone arch reaching into the sea
questions.imageCredit: Falaise d'Aval, Étretat · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: The chalk cliffs and natural arch of Étretat, painted many times by Monet and Courbet.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: A large double-walled medieval fortified city with pointed towers on a hill
questions.imageCredit: Cité de Carcassonne · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: The restored medieval Cité de Carcassonne, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: A tree-lined canal in an alpine town with mountains behind
questions.imageCredit: Canal du Vassé, Annecy · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: Annecy, the 'Venice of the Alps', on the shore of its famously clear lake.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: An enormous medieval Gothic stone palace with battlemented towers
questions.imageCredit: Palais des Papes, Avignon · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: The Palais des Papes in Avignon, the largest Gothic palace in Europe.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: A granite walled seaside town behind stone ramparts
questions.imageCredit: Saint-Malo intra-muros · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: The corsair city of Saint-Malo, ringed by ramparts and lashed by some of Europe's biggest tides.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: An enormous sand dune meeting a pine forest and the sea
questions.imageCredit: Dune du Pilat · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: The Dune du Pilat near Arcachon, the tallest sand dune in Europe.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: Colourful half-timbered houses lining a small canal
questions.imageCredit: Petite Venise, Colmar · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: The 'Petite Venise' canal quarter of Colmar, in Alsace.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: A cliff-top old town perched on tall white limestone sea cliffs
questions.imageCredit: Bonifacio · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: The clifftop citadel of Bonifacio, on the southern tip of the island, facing Sardinia.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: The long ornate golden-gated façade of a vast royal palace
questions.imageCredit: Palace of Versailles · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: The Palace of Versailles, Louis XIV's seat of power just west of Paris.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: A courtyard building with a steep roof of brightly patterned glazed tiles
questions.imageCredit: Hôtel-Dieu, Beaune · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: The Hospices de Beaune, with its famous polychrome glazed-tile roof, in the heart of Burgundy's wine country.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: A grand Flemish-style town square with ornate gabled buildings
questions.imageCredit: Grand'Place, Lille · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: The Grand'Place of Lille, its Flemish architecture a reminder of the region's ties to Belgium.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: A moated white stone castle with round towers in a city
questions.imageCredit: Château des ducs de Bretagne, Nantes · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: A twist: this is the Château des ducs de Bretagne in Nantes — historic capital of Brittany, but today in the Pays de la Loire, which still rankles some Bretons. Both answers accepted.
